baseline_context.note: The 226 count uses rustfmt's default standalone-file edition. Corpus governance uses the generated Cargo project's canonical edition-2024 check.

findings.title: The generated-code corpus is representative rather than exhaustive
findings.mechanism: The manifest pins selected entries and does not discover every emitted entrypoint and checked-in generated companion.

findings.title: Most checked-in demo emission is not rustfmt-clean
findings.mechanism: At the baseline, rustfmt --check rejects 226 of 265 demos/**/emitted.rs files.

findings.title: The generated Clippy gate suppresses broad emitter debt
findings.mechanism: GENERATED_CLIPPY_ARGS contains 68 -A flags, including ptr_arg, needless_return, map_identity, clone_on_copy, unreachable_code, and ordinary warning classes.

findings.title: The panic scanner misses user-triggerable crash mechanisms
findings.mechanism: The token scan covers unwrap, expect, panic, todo, unimplemented, unsafe, and allow, but not unreachable, abort, exit, indexing, arithmetic overflow, allocation casts, or capacity overflow.

findings.title: Generated rustfmt validation can normalize before checking
findings.mechanism: The quality path permits formatting generated projects before the check, so a producer that emits unformatted Rust can pass.

findings.title: Canonical int representation is split between i64 and SifrInt
findings.mechanism: General Type::Int lowering remains i64 while selected large constants and analyzed paths use SifrInt, producing representation-dependent semantics.

findings.title: Ordinary integer arithmetic can depend on Rust overflow mode
findings.mechanism: i64 arithmetic is emitted directly for paths outside selective SifrInt promotion, allowing debug panic and release wrapping to diverge.

findings.title: safe_math was reported as universal benchmark runtime code
findings.mechanism: The external report generalized a benchmark helper or generated artifact to every canonical emitted crate; the repository's maintained emitter does not install one universal safe_math.rs body in every program.
findings.rejection_reason: The universal-count claim is not reproducible. Its underlying integer division and modulo semantics are already owned by arithmetic lowering.

findings.title: Impossible states are discharged inside emitted user code
findings.mechanism: Baseline demo emission contains 2,098 unreachable! macros, 5 process aborts, and 8 process exits rather than one checked error model.

findings.title: Error-producing expressions use inconsistent fallback and termination paths
findings.mechanism: Division, decimal construction, dictionary proof discharge, and value-expression failures use unreachable, exit, abort, or fallback values instead of one typed checked path.

semantic_anchor.contains: unreachable!("sifr union narrowing fell through exhaustive branch chain")

findings.title: Collection reads bypass checked lowering on some paths
findings.mechanism: Direct Rust indexing coexists with guarded access, including nested access and lowering-specific paths.

findings.title: Out-of-range collection writes can silently do nothing
findings.mechanism: Some assignment lowering guards mutation with get_mut/if-let and omits the required IndexError branch.

findings.title: Star-unpack lowering can underflow or index before cardinality validation
findings.mechanism: Generated unpack expressions derive tail indices from len before one shared checked cardinality plan.

findings.title: Read-only dictionary membership was reported to insert defaults
findings.mechanism: Current membership lowering uses contains-style operations; or_insert occurrences serve mutation/default construction paths and do not establish a corpus-wide read mutation.
findings.rejection_reason: The cited mechanism is not reproducible as a read-only membership lowering defect. Collection-access regression coverage proves this invariant with a regression.

findings.title: Generators are materialized eagerly
findings.mechanism: Generator lowering buffers yielded values in Vec-backed output instead of preserving resumable execution.

findings.title: Infinite count iteration is capped at a finite prefix
findings.mechanism: The count() implementation delegates to count_from(start, step, 10000), so an API that must be unbounded stops after a fixed finite prefix.

findings.title: Invalid islice steps are adapted instead of rejected
findings.mechanism: The islice implementation rewrites a non-positive stride to one and truncates the stop boundary to the start instead of raising the canonical error.

findings.title: Signed string widths can become enormous usize allocations
findings.mechanism: ljust, rjust, zfill, and center lower signed widths through unchecked usize conversion before allocation.

findings.title: IO error rewrapping loses the original error kind
findings.mechanism: Generated try/except and IO adapters reconstruct IOError with a generic category instead of preserving the source kind.

findings.title: read_bytes size is not honored consistently
findings.mechanism: The generated file-handle read_bytes adapter can consume the full remaining stream regardless of the requested size.

findings.title: Decimal precision silently falls back in a live user path
findings.mechanism: BigDecimal default-context lowering calls with_prec(28) and silently falls back to the unmodified default context when precision construction fails.

findings.title: Generated APIs overuse owned collection and string references
findings.mechanism: Baseline demos contain 11,243 &String and 2,875 &Vec occurrences where str and slices or owned values are generally the idiomatic boundary.

findings.title: Clone insertion is excessive and sometimes compounds recursively
findings.mechanism: Baseline demos contain 9,853 clone calls and 1,079 cloned calls, including clone-then-borrow, clone-on-copy, full-row/container copies, and deep recursive traversal copies.

findings.title: Emission retains dead tails, identity transforms, and needless ceremony
findings.mechanism: Generated output includes unreachable statements after terminators, needless returns, identity maps, redundant closures, constant branches, and repeated formatting scaffolds.
findings.resolution: Canonicalization routes typed Rust IR through canonical control-flow and dead-binding passes, then parses the fully assembled file as a syn syntax tree for fixed-point demand, syntax, identifier, and API cleanup before final rendering. Focused structural and generated-shape regressions cover dead tails, identity transforms, constant branches, formatting scaffolds, and liveness-sensitive preservation.

findings.title: Baseline legacy generated main.rs snapshots were stale or mislabeled
findings.mechanism: At the audit baseline, fifteen demo main.rs files coexisted with canonical emitted.rs companions; at least two contained data-dependent unwrap or unrelated pasted output and were not governed by freshness checks.
findings.resolution: Corpus cleanup removed all fifteen legacy main.rs files. This inventory retains this baseline finding for provenance and confirms that the current authoritative producer owns only emitted.rs companions.

findings.title: The repository has no checked-in golden emitted Rust
findings.mechanism: The external report contradicted the 265 checked-in demos/**/emitted.rs companions present at the audit baseline.
findings.rejection_reason: Golden-like output exists; the real defects were incomplete freshness, coverage, formatting, and semantic governance, owned by corpus governance and canonicalization.
findings.resolution: The current surface intentionally contains 261 authoritative emitted.rs companions. Test-project idiomatic.rs references without a single-file emitted.rs producer remain explicitly non-authoritative, and the stale protocol_bounds idiomatic.rs reference was retired during canonicalization cleanup.

findings.title: Unicode string lowering repeatedly materializes and rescans characters
findings.mechanism: Baseline emission contains 937 Vec<char> mentions and uses chars().nth/count plus one-character String allocation in indexed and comparison-heavy paths.

findings.title: Collection lowering can worsen source algorithmic complexity
findings.mechanism: Container/row cloning, vector front removal, clone-swapping sorts, and repeated length/index work can turn linear or n-log-n source shapes into quadratic allocation and time.

findings.title: Every reported pop(0) site is a direct .remove(0) token
findings.mechanism: The exact token count is not reproducible in baseline emitted.rs, but front-removal semantics and equivalent vector-shift lowerings remain a verified complexity class.
findings.qualification: Own the semantic complexity mechanism, not the report's literal token count.

findings.title: Generated support and stdlib bridges can be emitted more than once
findings.mechanism: Project/module assembly must merge typed support demand before one canonical render, reject conflicting bridge bodies, and omit support that has no final consumer.

findings.title: Generated Cargo projects can embed machine-specific absolute paths
findings.mechanism: Local dependency and sysroot materialization can appear directly in generated manifests, making retained emitted projects host-specific.

findings.title: Compiler lowering introduces shell injection for string concatenation
findings.mechanism: The cited rm -rf concatenation is user-authored shell behavior rather than a compiler-introduced loss of argument boundaries.
findings.rejection_reason: No emitter-specific injection mechanism was demonstrated. Portability regression coverage proves that non-shell process APIs never acquire shell parsing during lowering.

findings.title: Unchecked signed-to-usize and capacity calculations threaten portability and safety
findings.mechanism: Nonliteral RustExpr::Cast nodes targeting usize render through sifr_runtime::to_usize_proven. The runtime conversion panics on an invalid bound proof, so generated index and allocation-count callers retain an obligation to establish non-negative, addressable bounds before narrowing.
findings.qualification: The former list.insert anchor is obsolete: lower_insert now calls exact_int_to_bound_expr, which emits clamp_slice_bound against the receiver length. This row instead anchors the remaining renderer/runtime proof boundary. Reconciliation preserves the confirmed blocking portability disposition; it neither establishes a new failing caller nor certifies all index and capacity proofs or targets.
